title: Local proxy fallback decision tree sketch
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal sketch for a local client-side proxy (or edge sidecar) that can perform fast, deterministic fallback decisions when upstream Redwood inference endpoints are slow/unavailable. The aim: minimize p99 client-visible latency regressions while preserving correctness and providing observability hooks.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Do not silently degrade to a lower-quality model without a signal and metric tradeoff.
- Prefer fast, cached partial answers over blocking long tail upstream timeouts.
- Expose a simple decision tree that can be overridden by policy flags.
- Emit telemetry events for every fallback decision.

Assumptions:
- Client runs a tiny local proxy (JS/Go) that can: cache responses, serve a small local LRU prefix store, and call upstream hosted/Dedicated endpoints.
- Upstream responses include: model_id, model_variant, token_count, latency_ms, and an optional quality_score hint (if provided by server).
- There is a configuration layer (file or bootstrap config from control plane) with policy flags.

High level decision tree (ASCII):

      incoming request
            |
            v
     check local policy/whitelist? ---- no ----> forward upstream (fast path)
            |yes
            v
   check recent/kv cache (exact key match) -- hit --> serve cached (telemetry: cache_hit)
            |miss
            v
   if small request && prewarm available? -- yes --> serve prewarm partial (telemetry: prewarm_used)
            |no
            v
   start upstream call (optimistic) and start local timeout T_local (configurable)
            |
   upstream responds before T_local --> normalize & return (telemetry: upstream_ok)
            |timeout
            v
   fallback selection: (see heuristics below)
            |
            v
   serve fallback response (cached/cheap model/partial) and concurrently let upstream finish and emit reconciliation event

Failure modes to consider:
- upstream eventually returns a conflicting answer (reconciliation needed)
- client receives partial or lower-quality output and must surface explanation (UI hint)
- repeated fallbacks for same tenant -> escalate to rate-limit or circuit-breaker

Heuristics matrix (config knobs):
- T_local: local cutoff before serving fallback (default 250ms for chat, 150ms for embed-only requests)
- fallback_tier: [cache_exact, cache_prefix, small_lm_local, tiny_local_llm, tos_limited_stub] ordered by preference
- quality_threshold: only serve fallback_tier if expected_quality >= threshold (if server provides quality hints)
- tenant_sensitivity: per-tenant thresholds (enterprise tenants get more conservative fallbacks)
- degrade_grace: allow N fallbacks/min before opening circuit for tenant

Example config (YAML sketch):

fallback_policy:
  default_T_local_ms: 250
  per_route_overrides:
    /v1/chat/completions:
      T_local_ms: 200
      fallback_tier: [cache_exact, small_lm_local, cached_prefix]
    /v1/embeddings:
      T_local_ms: 120
      fallback_tier: [cache_exact, tiny_local_embed]
  tenant_overrides:
    tenant_abc:
      quality_threshold: 0.85
      degrade_grace: 2

Telemetry events (emit on each decision):
- proxy.request.received {route, tenant, request_id}
- proxy.cache.check {key, hit:true/false, latency_ms}
- proxy.upstream.call {upstream_model, request_id, start_ts}
- proxy.upstream.response {latency_ms, success, model_variant}
- proxy.fallback.invoked {tier, reason, T_local_ms, tenant}
- proxy.reconciliation {fallback_response_id, upstream_response_id, delta_type}
- proxy.circuit.opened {tenant, window_seconds}

Fallback tiers (concrete ideas):
- cache_exact: return exact request match from local LRU cache. Fastest, safest.
- cache_prefix: use prefix/KV caching to supply continuation or short answer snippets (used for multi-turn chat). Needs safety checks.
- small_lm_local: onboard a tiny quantized 1-2B model optimized for short completions (e.g., summary/intent).
- tiny_local_llm: extremely small on-device distilled model for single-sentence answers (500M-1B).
- tos_limited_stub: deterministic constrained stub response ("Sorry, we are having trouble; please try again") used only if policy forbids lower-quality LMs.

API shapes and markers to support this (server-side instrumentation recommended):
- Upstream should include: \"x-model-quality-hint\": \"0.78\" and \"x-response-granularity\": \"full|partial|stub\" headers. This helps the proxy decide.
- Upstream streaming: proxy must be able to consume first N tokens quickly and decide if partial can be surfaced. Add meta token boundary markers to allow safe early exit.

Pseudocode (simplified):

func handleReq(req):
  emit(\"proxy.request.received\")
  if inWhitelist(req) and cache.has(req.key):
    emit(\"proxy.cache.check\", {hit:true})
    return cache.get(req.key)
  start upstream call async
  wait for either upstream or local timeout T_local
  if upstream returned:
    emit(\"proxy.upstream.response\", {success:true})
    maybeCache(resp)
    return resp
  // upstream slow or failed
  tier = chooseFallbackTier(req, tenant_config)
  resp = serveFallback(tier, req)
  emit(\"proxy.fallback.invoked\", {tier:tier})
  // let upstream finish and reconcile later
  spawn reconcile(upstream_call, resp)
  return resp

chooseFallbackTier heuristics: favours cached tiers unless request type disallows; respects tenant_quality_threshold and per-route rules. If model hint exists and < threshold, do not pick small_lm_local.

Reconciliation strategy (best-effort):
- When upstream returns, compute a delta fingerprint: short hash of semantics (n-gram or embedding distance).
- If delta > threshold, emit proxy.reconciliation event and optionally push a correction attempt to client (UI: non-blocking toast asking to refresh).
- For chats: stash upstream content and attach as \"late_message\" in next conversation sync packet. Avoid rewriting past responses in-place to not confuse UI.

Testing checklist (manual + unit/integration):
- unit tests for each fallback_tier selection with mocked upstream latencies and quality_hints
- fuzz tests: random drop upstream packets, ensure reconcilers handle late arrivals
- load test with thousands of small requests to validate false-positive circuit opens
- SLOs: ensure p95 latency improves for clients with proxy enabled without raising N+1 upstream calls

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to securely propagate tenant policy to ephemeral local proxy without leaking secrets? Option: control-plane signed policy tokens with expiry.
- Are we comfortable shipping a small LLM binary in the default client bundle? Consider lazy download with integrity verification.
- UX contract for showing fallback: how verbose should UI be? opt-in telemetry sharing?
- Cost accounting: if proxy falls back to tiny_local_llm and produces a token stream, how to attribute costs and quality?
- Combine with server-side automatic fallback: need consistent labels so the client and server don't double-fallback.

Implementation notes (practical):
- Keep the proxy binary tiny: Go + single static lib for inference or use wasm for tiny models.
- Keep cache eviction conservative for multi-turn sessions: prefer keeping last N turns.
- Provide a feature flag to force upstream-only mode for troubleshooting.

Short-term milestones:
- v0: sketch + unit tests for decision tree + telemetry schema (2 weeks)
- v1: basic JS/Go proxy with cache_exact and T_local behavior + reconciliation events (6 weeks)
- v2: add small_lm_local optional artifact and per-tenant policies (12 weeks)

Notes to self:
- Sync with Diego on telemetry names (we might prefer OTEL semantic conventions).
- Rina suggested adding a \"confidence_hint\" field to each cached entry to avoid cycling low-quality fallbacks. Good idea.

End of sketch.
